Title: Dronefall
BodyText: Dronefall is a visually captivating, interactive scrollytelling website designed by Artycoders and Anastasiia Hodubiak. It explores themes of technology, defense, and urgency in response to wartime realities. The pixel art style, retro aesthetics, and animated elements combine to create a compelling narrative experience, raising awareness and encouraging drone donations for Ukrainian defense.

Title: Aisen Caro Chacin
Description: Artist, creative technologist, researcher (Venezuela, USA, Spain)
BodyText: Aisen Caro Chacin is a regenerating composition of cells that produce a woman, a Venezuelan, a Spaniard, a U.S. American, and an animal whose patterns of migration are not based on seasons, but rather chance, chaos, and opportunity. She leads the medical prototyping lab at the University of Texas Medical Branch and is an Assistant Professor in Pathology at the School of Medicine. She is also Adjunct Faculty at the University of Houston’s School of Art and a founding board member of the Medicine and Arts Program at UCLA. With an MFA in Design and Technology from Parsons, and a Ph.D. in Human Informatics from the University of Tsukuba, Japan, Dr. Chacin’s work explores sensory perception, the human-machine relationship, embodiment, and incorporation through artificial bodies and realities in an era of conscious evolution. Her practice spans new media art, human-computer interfaces, medical devices, and Assistive Device Art (ADA), addressing topics such as sensory substitution, resuscitation, human echolocation, haptics, medical automation, surgical simulation, and fashion. Her work has been exhibited internationally at venues including Ars Electronica, Cite du Design, TEI, NIME, NYC Museum of Art and Design, The New York Hall of Science, and the Contemporary Arts Museum Houston. Featured in Future Tech by Discovery Channel, Creative Applications, FastCo, Time Techland, Engadget, and NY Times, she was also awarded and published by PopSci.

Title: Zach Lieberman – Daily Sketches in 2016
BodyText: Zach Lieberman is a renowned artist and educator known for using code to create dynamic, interactive, and generative art. His project “Daily Sketches in 2016” is a year-long creative exploration in which he published a generative drawing or interactive visual experiment every single day throughout 2016. These daily sketches demonstrate his commitment to the creative process, showcasing a wide range of styles, from fluid organic animations to geometric forms and playful interactions. The project stands as an inspiring example of how consistent practice and computational design can create a stunning, ever-evolving body of work that transcends traditional drawing.

Title: Shishi Yamazaki
BodyText: Shishi Yamazaki is a Tokyo-based animator and visual artist known for her distinctive blend of hand-drawn, watercolor-style animation and digital collage. Her work often features whimsical, surreal narratives populated by self-portraits and playful figures, exploring identity and transformation. She gained international attention with her short film “YA-NE-SEN a Go Go” (2011), which celebrates Tokyo’s Yanesen neighborhood through her lively, fluid animation style. Shishi’s commercial work includes projects for brands like Shiseido, Comme des Garçons, and her own personal experiments that push the boundaries of contemporary animation. Her style blends softness with a kinetic energy, combining traditional techniques with modern technology to produce vibrant, dreamlike visuals.

Title: Monopo Tokyo – AR Instagram Filters
BodyText: Monopo Tokyo is a Tokyo-based creative studio known for blending contemporary Japanese design aesthetics with global digital storytelling. Their Instagram AR filters and effects showcase their playful, experimental approach to interaction. These AR projects invite users to explore layered, dynamic designs that expand the narrative potential of social media platforms, reflecting Monopo Tokyo’s signature fusion of minimalism and motion.

Title: Runway – The Finance Platform Your Team Doesn’t Hate
BodyText: Reform Collective partnered with Runway Financial to craft a new identity and website that has users running to grab a window seat. Drawing inspiration from airport signage, wayfinding, and the air flight experience, the team created a first-class brand that stands out from the crowd. The project blends art direction, branding, web design, and web development to create a sleek, functional, and engaging digital presence for Runway.
